hook.text: Not everyone speaks an Indo-European language—Mandarin, Arabic, and Swahili belong to entirely different families.

buildup.text: Major families include Sino-Tibetan, Afro-Asiatic, Niger-Congo, Austronesian, and many more.

discovery.text: Niger-Congo is the largest by number of languages—over 1,500 members across Africa.

twist.text: Some languages like Basque, Korean, and Ainu have no confirmed relatives—linguistic orphans.

climax.text: The world has roughly 150 established language families—with many relationships still debated.

punchline.text: Languages have family trees—some are lone branches.

quiz.question: Which language family has the most individual languages?
